basis: Fixes the one blocking finding and the three non-blocking findings of the CTO review of 7b61b30 on AFC-241 (verdict CHANGES REQUESTED). BLOCKING: _audit_callers() flagged a CORRECT one-argument caller carrying ordinary shell punctuation -- the live .github/workflows/ci.yml:135 goes red on `--check-commit "$range" && echo "R2 gate done"` when it passes exactly one argument. Two causes in the argument counter, both fixed: `&` was absent from the metacharacter class, so `&&` and a bare `&` were scanned as ordinary tokens and everything after them counted as arguments; and a `break` did not discard the pending token, so the `2` of a `2>&1` counted as an argument even though `>` had stopped the scan. A token immediately before a metacharacter is a redirection, never an argument. NON-BLOCKING 1: the dispatcher's --check-commit branch now REFUSES a surplus argument with exit 2 instead of silently ignoring it, so the arity contract is enforced at the boundary rather than only one layer above it by the audit. NON-BLOCKING 2: CHECK_COMMIT_MAX_ARGS is now read by that branch, so the constant is bound to the code that honours it rather than to a human reader; assertion 11i pins the dispatcher from one side and 11f pins the constant from the other, so neither half can move alone. NON-BLOCKING 3: the function header now lists the COMPLETE set of shapes the audit does not cover, measured against 15: single-line `run:` and `- run:` prefixes, `sudo` and `env` prefixes, line continuations, a shell-function wrapper, `eval`, a package.json script string, and UNQUOTED command substitution as the first argument ( `(` is a metacharacter so the scan stops there and any argument after it is uncounted; quoting is counted correctly and is the form this repository uses). Unstated limits are the ones that mislead; a documented limit is a decision. NEW ASSERTIONS 11h and 11i plant the reviewer's shapes in BOTH directions -- eight correct one-argument callers with `&&`, `|`, `;`, `||`, `>` and `2>&1` attached must come back unflagged, and five two-argument callers with the same punctuation must still be caught. Fixing the false positives by loosening the scan would pass the first half and fail the second, which is the only way to make the assertion real; 11g previously proved only that prose is not flagged and that a bare one-argument caller is counted, and that omission was the whole of the review finding. VERIFIED: --self-test 32 assertions exit 0; the reviewer's 11-shape table reproduced exactly, all eleven matching; four mutants each caught by a named assertion -- `&` removed from the class, pending token not discarded on break, dispatcher widened with the constant untouched (11i red), constant raised to 2 with the dispatcher untouched (11f and 11h and 11i red). Unchanged: GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS byte-identical to 7b61b30; --check-commit 84e65f7 and 65e7631 exit 1; not-a-revision exit 2. No change to scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh or scripts/run-db-tests.mjs, no migration, no engine change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged. This claim carries no Reviewed-by trailer: the commit is UNREVIEWED and is raised to MediaTech (CTO). There is no independent security reviewer on this team -- that seat was declined by the board on cost -- so a CTO self-review is a recorded degradation, not independent review.
